note: Independent rejudgment at HEAD 6f076fc22d of the {partial} row d7673ff783 recorded. draft-ietf-bess-mup-safi-01 Section 3.1.3.1 (rfc/drafts/draft-ietf-bess-mup-safi.txt): "- < 0:   the mandatory fields exceed the declared Length; the NLRI is malformed; MUST be treated as Treat-as-withdraw." The same section: "The Source Address Length has a fixed length of 1 octet." Tested: "mandatory fields exceed the declared Length", scoped by the Reason to a declared Length ending inside the Endpoint Address, complete mandatory fields the accepted control. Gap: "MUST be treated as Treat-as-withdraw", for a draft-mpmz-bess-mup-safi-02 Type 1 ST route ending exactly at its Endpoint Address, which lacks the mandatory Source Address Length octet. Producer: internal/component/bgp/plugins/nlri/mup/types.go::parseBodyT1ST, whose len(rest)==0 branch after the endpoint sets sourceBits=0 and sourceOctetAbsent=true and returns nil instead of ErrMUPTruncated; the route is then held and relayed with the octet added (canonical.go canonicalT1STGrow/writeCanonicalT1ST, observed by reactor/t1st_02_relay_test.go TestMUPT1ST02RelayedWithSourceLength). The gap is therefore real, not a disclosure of untested code. It is the owner decision of 2026-10-22 recorded in plan/release/fixes/spec-exabgp-6-api-compatibility.md (follow ExaBGP f9bfb853b: 'a -02 MUP Type 1 ST route without Source Address Length read as length 0'), a deliberate deviation never counted as conformant. Letter: violated for the -02 shape. Spirit: the rule exists so a parser never reads mandatory fields out of the octets past the Length; the -02 read consumes nothing past the Length, so framing stays sound, but a missing mandatory field is supplied by assumption, which the draft forbids. Tested scope, four questions: (1) TestMUPT1STMandatoryFieldsWithinLength (nlri/mup/draft_ietf_bess_mup_safi_tlv_mup_test.go) asserts ErrorIs ErrMUPTruncated for t1stBody cut by 3 octets (Source Address Length plus 2 endpoint octets), positive asserts NoError, empty remainder, exact TEID 0x3039 and endpoint 10.0.0.1; TestMUPMalformedT1STTreatAsWithdraw (reactor/draft_ietf_bess_mup_safi_t1st_withdraw_test.go) holds well-formed K0, receives the same key with its endpoint cut by 2 octets between siblings L and L2 (L2 with unknown TLV 0xF0), and asserts ActionNone, MP_REACH equal to exactly L||L2, MP_UNREACH equal to exactly K0 and decodable by the registered recognizer; its negative asserts a well-formed UPDATE returns byte-identical. That is treat-as-withdraw per RFC 7606 Section 2, what the draft says, not merely what the code does. (2) Exact ErrorIs and byte-exact section assertions fail on a mutant that returns nil, reads the endpoint short, or widens the -02 tolerance to a mid-endpoint stop; the recorded discrimination is only a revert (panic) break of parseBodyT1ST and ValidateNLRI, which proves the units exercise the producers, not this branch, so question 2 rests on this reading. (3) Isolated: TEID 1/0x3039 nonzero, Endpoint Address Length 32 valid, only the truncation fires; siblings well formed. (4) Whole requirement: no. Besides the -02 gap, truncation inside the prefix, inside TEID/QFI/Endpoint Address Length, and inside a non-zero Source Address all reach ErrMUPTruncated in parseBodyT1ST/parsePrefixField but are tagged by neither unit: implemented, unverified under this row, and given no credit. Polarity labels differ between the two units (parser: negative = truncated; reactor: positive = truncated withdrawn), each pair is a distinct conforming/violating input, not one assertion in two hats. Partial stands, zero whole-requirement credit.
